items.q: Describe what your company does in 50 characters or less.
items.a: Predicts berth delays at container terminals

items.q: What is your company going to make? Please describe your product and what it does or will do.
items.a:
Tidewater predicts berth delays at container terminals 72 hours ahead, using ship positions (AIS), weather and crane schedules. The forecast is live at 2 terminals in Rotterdam.

Today planners rebuild the berth plan by hand every shift. Next we will re-plan the schedule automatically when a delay is predicted.
items.tl: Berth-delay forecasts 72 h ahead, live at 2 terminals in Rotterdam.

items.a: 14 planners use Tidewater every shift (daily actives) at 2 terminals in Rotterdam. The delay forecast is live; automatic re-planning is next. First paid pilot signed in October at EUR 4k/month.
items.tl: 14 daily active planners at 2 terminals, first paid pilot EUR 4k/month.

items.q: Why did you pick this idea to work on?
items.a: Maya ran berth planning at a terminal for 5 years and watched every plan break by noon. Leo spent 4 years as a backend engineer at a freight-tracking startup.
items.tl: Maya ran berth planning for 5 years; Leo built freight tracking for 4.
